heading: INT. PARKED CAR - ABANDONED QUARRY - NIGHT

units.text: INT. PARKED CAR - ABANDONED QUARRY - NIGHT
A small digital recorder sits in the cupholder, its red light steady.
DETECTIVE SERAPHINA OKONJO-WYATT (40s, rain-slick trench, eyes that haven't slept in days) leans toward the recorder.
This is Detective Okonjo-Wyatt. Eleventh of November, twenty-three-forty. If anyone is listening to this, I'm sorry.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: Then, on the tape, her own voice plays back from earlier.
Monday. The body was found at the foot of the quarry stairs. No wallet. No phone. One shoe.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: The shoe was wrong. Left shoe, size nine, on a right foot. I should have seen it Monday. I saw it Wednesday. Wednesday is too late.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: The man in the stairwell wasn't the man we buried. The man we buried was a second man, and the second man had been dead since Friday. The first man is alive. He is walking around in the first man's shoes.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: His name is Corwin Hale. He's the one who called it in.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: Corwin Hale found the body at dawn. He said he was jogging. He was in loafers.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: Loafers, Corwin. I wrote it down. You saw me write it down.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: Beyond the glass, in the rain, a pair of headlights is turning in at the quarry gate, slowly, very slowly.
If this is the last thing I record, I want it noted that I was right.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: She does not look at them.
She reaches out and presses the recorder once more.
Case file is in the glove box. The key is under the seat. Tell Marguerite I did love her.
units.name: SERAPHINA

units.text: Her shadow lunges across the dashboard.
